source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne Chandler campus spans eight buildings, labeled PHX1 through PHX8, at a single address on South Ellis Street, with 169 MW of published IT capacity across 2,000,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 169 MW supports roughly 4,225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise density, the same power supports roughly 16,900 racks. Those are assumptions about density, not CyrusOne's claims. The eight-building structure suggests the campus grew incrementally, which is consistent with operators adding shells as demand and power agreements are secured rather than delivering all capacity at once.

The certifications qualify this campus to host regulated workloads across several domains. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial and operational controls audited over time. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 is an internationally recognized information security management standard. FISMA qualifies it for certain federal government workloads. TIA-942 is a data center infrastructure standard covering design and build quality. Green Globes is an environmental performance rating. No tenants are named in the published specifications.

Within Arizona, this site ranks first by published IT capacity among the 56 facilities this site has mapped in the state, and it accounts for all 169 MW of published capacity in the state total, because it is the only facility among those 56 for which an operator spec page reviewed here has published a megawatt figure. That means the ranking reflects the limits of published data, not a complete survey of Arizona capacity. Arizona sits in a region where power and water constraints on data center growth are active policy topics, but no grid or utility figures for this campus are published in the specifications reviewed here.
